config.title: WebSocket Hook

intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook that manages a WebSocket connection. You will learn how to use the useEffect hook to establish and clean up a WebSocket, and the useState hook to store and update real-time messages. The main technologies involved are React hooks, the WebSocket API, and event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can connect to a WebSocket server and handle incoming data.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll see them powering live chat interfaces like Slack or Discord, where messages appear instantly without page refreshes. They're also crucial for financial dashboards displaying live stock prices, collaborative editing tools like Google Docs showing real-time cursor positions, and multiplayer game interfaces updating player movements immediately. As a developer, implementing WebSocket hooks lets you create responsive, interactive experiences that feel alive and connected.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook to manage WebSocket connections
Initialize WebSocket connections with dynamic URL parameters
Control WebSocket lifecycle events (open, message, close, error) within React components
Manipulate component state based on real-time WebSocket data
Bind WebSocket event handlers to update UI components
Integrate the WebSocket hook into a functional React component
Configure message sending and receiving through the custom hook interface
Apply cleanup logic to properly close WebSocket connections on component unmount

steps.title: Import React and required hooks (useState, useEffect, useRef)
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the required hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React, useState, useEffect, and useRef are added to the file.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the necessary hooks for WebSocket functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure to import all four: React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the useWebSocket custom hook function
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named useWebSocket that takes a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a URL parameter and returns an object. For now, just return an empty object {}.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

// Create the useWebSocket custom hook function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useWebSocket function is defined that takes a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function is created with a URL parameter and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useWebSocket custom hook function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is named useWebSocket, accepts a URL parameter, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name, parameter, and return value.

steps.title: Initialize state for WebSocket connection status
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, use useState to create an 'isConnected' state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value false and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will have an isConnected state variable that tracks the WebSocket connection status.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function contains a useState call that creates an isConnected variable initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isConnected state variable to track the WebSocket connection status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with the correct initial value and destructuring pattern.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isConnected state variable wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState(false) inside the useWebSocket function.

steps.title: Initialize state for WebSocket messages
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, add a useState call to create a 'messages' state variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial value should be an empty array [].
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will have a 'messages' state variable ready to store incoming WebSocket messages.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket function contains a useState call that declares a 'messages' variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track WebSocket messages.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside useWebSocket, use useState to create a 'messages' state variable initialized to [].

steps.title: Create a ref to store the WebSocket instance
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, create a ref using useRef to store the WebSocket instance. Initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Use the useRef hook you imported earlier to create a reference that persists across renders.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket function will contain a socketRef variable created with useRef, initialized to null.
successCriteria: A socketRef variable is created using useRef and initialized to null inside the useWebSocket function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref to store the WebSocket instance. This will allow us to maintain a persistent reference to the WebSocket connection across component renders.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useRef to create the reference and initializing it to null inside the useWebSocket function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the useWebSocket function, use the useRef hook to create a reference for the WebSocket instance and set its initial value to null.

steps.title: Define the WebSocket connection handler
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, create a 'connect' function that creates a new WebSocket instance, stores it in socketRef, and sets up event listeners.
steps.hint: Define a function named 'connect' that creates a WebSocket instance with a URL, assigns it to socketRef.current, and adds event listeners for 'open', 'message', and 'close' events.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'connect' function is defined inside useWebSocket, which creates a WebSocket instance and sets up event listeners.
successCriteria: The 'connect' function is defined, creates a new WebSocket instance, assigns it to socketRef.current, and includes event listeners for 'open', 'message', and 'close'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the 'connect' function to establish a WebSocket connection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the 'connect' function, but it's missing some parts. Make sure it creates a WebSocket instance, stores it in socketRef, and sets up event listeners for 'open', 'message', and 'close'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'connect' function is not defined correctly. Ensure it's inside useWebSocket, creates a WebSocket instance, stores it in socketRef.current, and sets up event listeners.

steps.title: Define the WebSocket disconnection handler
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, create a function named 'disconnect' that closes the WebSocket connection if it exists and updates the connection state.
steps.hint: Check if the WebSocket instance stored in the ref exists, then call its close() method and set isConnected to false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useWebSocket hook now contains a disconnect function that properly closes the WebSocket connection and updates the connection status.
successCriteria: A disconnect function exists inside useWebSocket that checks for the WebSocket instance, calls close(), and updates isConnected state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the disconnect handler that will close the WebSocket connection when needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your disconnect function checks if the WebSocket instance exists, calls close() on it, and updates the isConnected state to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The disconnect function is missing or incomplete. It should check for the WebSocket instance, close the connection, and update the connection state.

steps.title: Implement useEffect to manage WebSocket lifecycle
steps.instruction: Inside the useWebSocket function, add a useEffect hook that calls the connect function when the component mounts and returns a cleanup function that calls the disconnect function.
steps.hint: The useEffect hook should have an empty dependency array to run only on mount, and return a function that calls disconnect.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added to manage WebSocket connection on mount and disconnection on unmount.
successCriteria: useEffect is implemented with an empty dependency array, calls connect inside, and returns a cleanup function that calls disconnect.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the useEffect hook to manage the WebSocket lifecycle.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your useEffect has an empty dependency array, calls connect, and returns a cleanup function that calls disconnect.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Review the useEffect syntax and ensure it handles both mount and unmount events.

steps.title: Return the hook's interface object
steps.instruction: Return an object from the useWebSocket hook containing isConnected, messages, and disconnect function so consuming components can access them.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use a return statement with an object containing the three values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now exposes its state and functionality through a returned object, making it ready for components to consume.
successCriteria: The useWebSocket hook returns an object containing isConnected, messages, and disconnect function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Your hook now properly exposes its interface to consuming components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with exactly isConnected, messages, and disconnect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't returning the required interface. Check that you're returning an object with the three properties.

steps.title: Create and export the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named WebSocketDemo that uses the useWebSocket hook and returns a basic JSX structure with a heading.
steps.hint: Define the component after the hook function, call useWebSocket inside it, and return JSX with an <h1> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named WebSocketDemo is created that calls useWebSocket and returns JSX with a heading.
successCriteria: The WebSocketDemo component is defined, uses the useWebSocket hook, and returns JSX containing an <h1> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the WebSocketDemo component that uses your custom hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it calls useWebSocket and returns JSX with a heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing or doesn't match the requirements. Create a component named WebSocketDemo that uses useWebSocket and returns JSX with a heading.
